title: Lior and the Harvest
premise: Emrys Quintana has spent seven years as a hospice nurse hearing the dying count backwards from ten, a sound she's rationalized into silence. When an excavation crew beneath the town of Lior unearths a stone door sealed from the inside, the counting spreads to the living — and Emrys discovers she is the last descendant of the town's founders, the bloodline that once sang the door shut. The song requires a chorus of townspeople to complete its final verse, but every voice that joins it is slowly erased and replaced by something that wears their memories. To reseal the door without losing herself or the people she loves, Emrys must learn the verse alone, conduct it through others without singing along herself, and accept that the price of belonging may be forgetting who she ever was.
about_author: Ines Vane is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who writes horror rooted in the strange intimacies of tending the dying. She lives in a coastal town with too many old churches and claims she can still hear her former patients humming.

chapters.title: Ten
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: during a hospice shift, patient Marisol counts backwards from ten and dies mid-three, whispering 'the door.' Emrys logs it as another coincidence, but the number follows her home in the pipes, the clock radio, a child skipping rope outside. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; the reader learns her seven-year habit of explaining things away.

chapters.title: The Door Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the excavation crew breaks ground on the hospice's expansion and unearths a basalt door with no handle, scratched shut from within. That night every dying patient in the county begins counting at once. Crew foreman Dov Kessler begs Emrys for help because his crew hears it loudest. Emotional beat: the collapse of her rationalizations; isolation begins.

chapters.title: What the Founders Sang
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: researching town archives, she finds her own surname among the founding families and a hymnal with a song missing its final verse, torn out deliberately. Her grandmother's letters describe 'keeping the count' as a family duty. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance; identity cracks open as she realizes the counting chose her bloodline.

chapters.title: The First Chorus
chapters.summary: Dov, POV: the trapped crew, unable to leave the site without the counting intensifying, begin humming fragments of the recovered melody involuntarily. One worker, Petra, sings a full line and afterward cannot remember her daughter's face. Emotional beat: power introduced as seduction — the song feels like relief before it takes payment.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the town, half-infected by the hum, grows eerily warm toward Emrys — casseroles, invitations, eyes that hold too long. She realizes they aren't welcoming her; the thing behind the door is recruiting through them, offering the belonging she's always lacked. Emotional beat: temptation; loneliness weaponized.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Emrys and Dov, alternating POV: they reconstruct the torn verse from Marisol's hospice recordings, where her backwards counting was actually the melody reversed. Each rehearsal costs someone a memory. Dov forgets his brother; Emrys starts losing small pieces of her childhood. Emotional beat: mounting sacrifice; the corruption of a tool meant to protect.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Petra, POV: inside the sealed chamber (via a dream-state), we see the previous generations who sang themselves into the door — including Emrys's grandmother, intact but hollowed, still conducting an eternal chorus. She warns: the last verse must be sung by many voices but owned by none. Emotional beat: revelation and grief; the true cost of the family duty.

chapters.title: Recruitment
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV: the town holds a festival that is transparently a mass audition for the chorus. The entity speaks through the mayor, offering Emrys her mother's voice back if she leads. Half the town signs up willingly, hungry for the warmth. Emotional beat: power's full corruption; Emrys must refuse the one thing she's always wanted.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, climax: at the door, with the excavated breach widening, Emrys conducts the completed song through volunteers who sing while she stays silent — biting her own tongue bloody to keep from joining. The door grinds shut as the singers dissolve into it smiling. Dov holds the line physically; Petra's remembered daughter's name becomes the final note. Emotional beat: terrible triumph; everything paid at once.

chapters.title: One
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, resolution: weeks later, the town remembers nothing, and neither fully does Emrys — she kept enough of herself to grieve what she gave. Back at the hospice, a new patient begins counting backwards, softly, and stops at one, waiting. Emrys picks up the hymnal and begins writing a new first verse. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity; belonging redefined as chosen vigilance rather than inherited blood.
